analysis.title: GSX POWER BACK ON, AMERICA (buy GSENEPOW)
key_insights: Faris Mourad's desk likes buying the Power Up America basket (GSENEPOW) here. The desk calls power the most underappreciated AI bottleneck, with low positioning, normalized valuation and intact fundamentals.

The theme has underperformed other AI themes and the S&P 500 YTD. The note attributes this to political and regulatory noise, not fundamentals: utility bill affordability before the November elections, state-level data center restrictions, grid reliability concerns and local NIMBY pushback.

Positioning in all Power Up America categories (Grid Infrastructure, Uranium/Nuclear, Natural Gas) is at about a 2-year low. IPP and GEV valuations (GSXUIPPS) are also at a 2-year low and near Liberation Day lows. Grid Infrastructure (GSXUGRID) valuations have reverted to January 2025 levels.

The desk expects potential incentives to increase US power supply through grid infrastructure spending and behind-the-meter solutions. It also expects higher earnings revisions as IPPs announce long-term partnerships with mega-cap tech.
Suggested implementation into year-end: sell the 31Dec 85% put to help fund a 110/135% call spread on GSENEPOW, for 1.75%.

Key dated catalysts: FERC ruling on the PJM large-load framework (Oct 12), PJM Reliability Backstop Procurement (RBP) filings, 3Q earnings updates, November midterms, and the ERCOT data center interconnection audit (finalizes about Dec 10).

CEG announced PPAs with Google for about 3.6 GW of nuclear in PJM, and a 20-year nuclear PPA for about 700 MW in PJM. CEG's share of nuclear capacity contracted under a PPA rose from 13% to 28%. CEG has the most capacity still available to contract.

GS research sees data center power demand of 108 GW by 2030 (23% CAGR off a 2025 base) and a 3.5% total US power demand CAGR through 2030. Data centers contribute just over 2.5% of that, split about 1.8% front-of-meter and 0.8% behind-the-meter. YTD US power demand is up about 3% YoY through July, with preliminary August data above 3%.

Utility affordability is the central policy issue (Carly Davenport). Average US utility bills are up about 14% over three years and have outpaced CPI since 2021. DC is up over 55%, Nevada down 18%. PJM bills are up over 24%, about 10 points above the US average.

Local pushback: Pennsylvania's executive order requires local community approvals before state permitting and sets binding standards. A Texas executive order has paused data center development pending an audit of the interconnection queue, with results expected around Dec 10. The analyst expects the noise to abate after the elections in most cases but remain an issue into 2027 legislative sessions.

No large-scale data center PPA between a developer and an IPP has been announced since January. PJM deal flow is gated by the FERC ruling, RBP filings and the midterms. In Texas, more deal announcements are expected after the Dec 10 audit.

GS research is selective on regulated utilities because of potentially tighter regulation where bill inflation is high. It is more constructive on IPPs, which are down about 30% over 12 months. CEG, NRG, TLN and VST trade at just over 7x EBITDA with a 12% free cash flow yield on 2027 estimates, both at the discounted end of historical ranges. PJM forward power curves continue to move higher, and near-term Texas power prices are weak.

Equipment demand (Joe Ritchie): GEV guides to 125 GW of backlog plus slot reservation agreements by year end, about 6x its current 20 GW capacity. Half of 2031 slots will be booked by year end and 2032 SRAs are already being taken. GEV takes about $100 million in deposits per HA turbine for 2031-2032 delivery. The CCGT market has grown from 20-30 GW to over 100 GW.

Interconnection queues of up to 4.5 years push developers toward behind-the-meter (BTM) gas engines and turbines. BTM is expected to be about 20% of data center power demand by 2030 (50-60 GW). Participants include INIO, CAT, Wartsila, Cummins, BKR and fuel cells (FCEL, BE). Ritchie views INNIO's technology as best in class for BTM.

Over-capacity is a legitimate concern later in the decade but not today: industry capacity is estimated at 90-100 GW, rising into 2028. GEV booked a record 2Q and Ritchie does not expect as many gigawatts booked this quarter (the second derivative turning), but backlog grows and service content on the installed base will be more profitable.

Construction (Adam Bubes): data center construction spending re-accelerated to +56-58% YoY in July, and August project starts were up about 250% YoY. Starts lead spending by about one year, and the 12-month value of starts is about 3x construction spending, giving at least two years of visibility. Announcements lead starts by about 200 days.

Announcement momentum has moderated: since July, total announced backlog is up only 1% sequentially and the high-probability announced-but-not-started backlog is down about 4%. MEP contractors book work about six months after groundbreaking, so the pipeline gives 12-18 months of bookings visibility.

Of roughly $1 trillion of data center capex, only about $70 billion goes to construction (9% of private non-residential construction). FIX is favored for its flexible labor, modular platform (about 17% of revenue) and Texas exposure. The top five states hold about 60% of capacity under construction. Virginia has slowed to high single digit growth after a Loudoun County approvals pause, and New York has a moratorium.

Gas infrastructure (Olivia Foster): US gas market is about 110 bcf/d and is expected to grow about 20% by 2030, split between data center power demand (10-11 bcf/d) and LNG/international demand (10-11 bcf/d). Top five pipeline systems for KMI and WMB ran above 90% utilization in 2025 versus about 70% a decade ago. Average backlog for KMI, WMB, TRP and DTM more than doubled from end-2023 to 2Q26, and pre-FID opportunities are more than double sanctioned backlog.

KMI, WMB, TRP and DTM are down 13% over three months versus -3% for the AMNA benchmark. Causes: state-level regulatory delays, higher interest rates, and Middle East conflict lifting crude and favoring oil pipeline names. State-level restrictions may increase preference for behind-the-meter power, a tailwind for WMB and KGS.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand forecasts were raised, GEV has 125 GW of backlog plus reservations (about 6x capacity), data center construction spending is up 56-58% YoY and starts are up about 250% YoY. Valuations and positioning are at 2-year lows.
tension_points.bear_case: Affordability politics, Texas and Pennsylvania restrictions, a 1% sequential rise in announced backlog since July, no large developer-IPP PPA since January, and a possible slowdown in GEV bookings.
tension_points.what_invalidates: FERC ruling on the PJM large-load framework (Oct 12), the Dec 10 ERCOT audit outcome, and the November midterms are the gating events. A continued absence of large data center PPAs would weaken the thesis.

theme_stances.key_argument: Positioning is low, valuation has normalized and the fundamentals are intact, so the desk likes buying the Power Up America basket.
theme_stances.evidence: This is the most underappreciated AI bottleneck.

theme_stances.key_argument: Pipeline utilization above 90% means every incremental molecule of demand needs new capacity, and backlogs have more than doubled.
theme_stances.evidence: every incremental molecule of downstream demand requires incremental pipeline capacity
